name: Knockma

mound of the fairy king Finnbheara
lived there with his bride Una, also called Nuala

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Knockma is an Irish mythological site. The hill rises near Tuam in County Galway. Its name recalls the queen Medb. Yet people know it as the mound of Finnbheara. He rules the west of Connacht, that land, as its fairy king. He dwelt there with his fairy bride Una, who is also called Nuala. The place is today known as Castle Hackett.
